profile.subtitleJa: ダビデがユダの王として拠点を置いた町。
profile.summaryJa: ダビデは神に尋ねた後、ユダの町々からヘブロンへ上ります。初出の本文は、ここを行き先としてのみ示します。

facts.textJa: イスラエルの長老たちはヘブロンでダビデと契約し、彼を王にしました。
アブサロムはヘブロンで自分を王と告げる合図を広めました。

profile.modernLocationJa: 古代のヘブロンは現代ヘブロンと重なる地域にありますが、古代範囲と現代市街地は同一ではありません。
profile.historicalRoleJa: ダビデが神に尋ね、ユダの町々から上る先として指定された町。
profile.locationNoteJa: 古代の範囲・正確な現代位置は、本文と確認済み資料だけでは一点に定められません。

wikipedia.title: Hebron
wikipedia.noteJa: 記事は、イスラエル人のヘブロンが現在のテル・ルメイダを中心としていたと記し、ダビデがそこへ移り治めたという2サムエル2:1–3も挙げます。古代の中心地と現在の市街地は区別されます。

primaryWitnesses.textualBasisJa: After this, David inquired of the LORD, saying, “Shall I go up into any of the cities of Judah?” The LORD said to him, “Go up.” David said, “Where shall I go up?” He said, “To Hebron.”
David brought up his men who were with him, every man with his household. They lived in the cities of Hebron.
The time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.
They took up Asahel and buried him in the tomb of his father, which was in Bethlehem. Joab and his men went all night, and the day broke on them at Hebron.
Sons were born to David in Hebron. His firstborn was Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess;
and the sixth, Ithream, of Eglah, David’s wife. These were born to David in Hebron.
Abner also spoke in the ears of Benjamin; and Abner went also to speak in the ears of David in Hebron all that seemed good to Israel and to the whole house of Benjamin.
So Abner came to David to Hebron, and twenty men with him. David made Abner and the men who were with him a feast.
Behold, David’s servants and Joab came from a raid and brought in a great plunder with them; but Abner was not with David in Hebron, for he had sent him away, and he had gone in peace.
When Abner had returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside into the middle of the gate to speak with him quietly, and struck him there in the body, so that he died for the blood of Asahel his brother.
They buried Abner in Hebron; and the king lifted up his voice and wept at Abner’s grave; and all the people wept.
When Saul’s son heard that Abner was dead in Hebron, his hands became feeble, and all the Israelites were troubled.

They brought the head of Ishbosheth to David to Hebron, and said to the king, “Behold, the head of Ishbosheth, the son of Saul, your enemy, who sought your life! The LORD has avenged my lord the king today of Saul and of his offspring.”

David commanded his young men, and they killed them, cut off their hands and their feet, and hanged them up beside the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ishbosheth and buried it in Abner’s grave in Hebron.
Then all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and spoke, saying, “Behold, we are your bone and your flesh.
So all the elders of Israel came to the king to Hebron, and King David made a covenant with them in Hebron before the LORD; and they anointed David king over Israel.
In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.
David took more concubines and wives for himself out of Jerusalem, after he had come from Hebron; and more sons and daughters were born to David.
At the end of forty years, Absalom said to the king, “Please let me go and pay my vow, which I have vowed to the LORD, in Hebron.
The king said to him, “Go in peace.” So he arose and went to Hebron.
But Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, “As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpet, then you shall say, ‘Absalom is king in Hebron!’”
